questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy with a lifelong history of easy bruising and prolonged bleeding presents with the painful, swollen knee highlighted in this photograph. What is the most likely cause of the swelling?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fat and marrow leakage from an occult fracture (lipohemarthrosis)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacterial infection of the joint (septic arthritis)

explanation.summary: Repeated spontaneous bleeding into weight-bearing joints such as the knees, ankles, and elbows (hemarthrosis) is a hallmark of hemophilia and, over time, produces chronic joint swelling, pain, and deformity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Repeated spontaneous bleeding into weight-bearing joints such as the knees, ankles, and elbows (hemarthrosis) is a hallmark of hemophilia and, over time, produces chronic joint swelling, pain, and deformity.

questions.stem: In this diagram of the clotting cascade, the two marked deficiencies (factor VIII and factor IX) both disrupt the same limb of coagulation. What pattern of routine coagulation studies would result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prolongation of both PT and aPTT

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prolonged PT with a normal aPTT

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged aPTT with a normal PT

choices.label: E
choices.text: Isolated prolonged bleeding time with normal aPTT

explanation.summary: Factors VIII and IX act in the intrinsic arm of the cascade, which is measured by the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT). Their deficiency therefore prolongs the aPTT while leaving the extrinsic-pathway-dependent PT normal.
explanation.whyCorrect: Factors VIII and IX act in the intrinsic arm of the cascade, which is measured by the activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT). Their deficiency therefore prolongs the aPTT while leaving the extrinsic-pathway-dependent PT normal.

questions.stem: This diagram traces how the gene defect underlying hemophilia A and B passes from an unaffected father and a carrier mother to their children. What inheritance pattern does it depict?

explanation.summary: Hemophilia A and B are X-linked recessive disorders. Sons of a carrier mother have a 50% chance of being affected, and daughters have a 50% chance of being carriers, which is why the disease predominantly affects males.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hemophilia A and B are X-linked recessive disorders. Sons of a carrier mother have a 50% chance of being affected, and daughters have a 50% chance of being carriers, which is why the disease predominantly affects males.

questions.stem: This diagram illustrates how the gene defect responsible for von Willebrand disease is most commonly passed from parents to offspring. Which mode of inheritance is depicted?

explanation.summary: The pedigree shows an affected parent transmitting the trait to roughly half of the children of either sex, with no skipping of generations and no sex predominance, which is the pattern of autosomal dominant inheritance. Most cases of von Willebrand disease follow this pattern, although rare autosomal recessive (e.g., type 3) forms exist.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pedigree shows an affected parent transmitting the trait to roughly half of the children of either sex, with no skipping of generations and no sex predominance, which is the pattern of autosomal dominant inheritance. Most cases of von Willebrand disease follow this pattern, although rare autosomal recessive (e.g., type 3) forms exist.

questions.stem: This clinical photograph shows a lacy, reticulated, mottled purplish-red skin discoloration on the lower limb of a patient. What is the underlying mechanism producing this skin finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Obstruction of superficial dermal capillaries by microthrombi

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dilation of superficial venules from hepatic dysfunction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immune complex deposition in vessel walls with leukocytoclastic vasculitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Extravasation of red cells from platelet-deficient capillaries

explanation.summary: The mottled, net-like discoloration is livedo reticularis, a characteristic skin manifestation of antiphospholipid antibody syndrome. It results from obstruction of small superficial capillaries by microthrombi, reflecting the prothrombotic state that also causes DVT, PE, stroke, and recurrent pregnancy loss.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mottled, net-like discoloration is livedo reticularis, a characteristic skin manifestation of antiphospholipid antibody syndrome. It results from obstruction of small superficial capillaries by microthrombi, reflecting the prothrombotic state that also causes DVT, PE, stroke, and recurrent pregnancy loss.

questions.stem: This patient developed sharply demarcated hemorrhagic skin necrosis on the thigh shortly after starting an oral anticoagulant. Which underlying deficiency most predisposes to this complication?

explanation.summary: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis occurs because protein C (a vitamin K-dependent factor with a short half-life) falls faster than the procoagulant factors after warfarin is started, producing a transient hypercoagulable state with microvascular thrombosis. It is characteristically seen in patients with underlying protein C deficiency; protein S deficiency rarely causes it.
explanation.whyCorrect: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis occurs because protein C (a vitamin K-dependent factor with a short half-life) falls faster than the procoagulant factors after warfarin is started, producing a transient hypercoagulable state with microvascular thrombosis. It is characteristically seen in patients with underlying protein C deficiency; protein S deficiency rarely causes it.

questions.stem: This schematic maps the coagulation cascade and highlights where the inherited thrombotic disorders act. In the group of disorders that BLOCK termination of thrombosis, which physiologic anticoagulant is depicted inactivating both factor Va and factor VIIIa?

explanation.summary: Activated protein C, using protein S as a cofactor, proteolytically inactivates factors Va and VIIIa to switch off the common pathway. Factor V Leiden resists this cleavage, and protein C or S deficiency removes this brake, both causing hypercoagulability. Antithrombin instead inhibits thrombin and factor Xa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Activated protein C, using protein S as a cofactor, proteolytically inactivates factors Va and VIIIa to switch off the common pathway. Factor V Leiden resists this cleavage, and protein C or S deficiency removes this brake, both causing hypercoagulability. Antithrombin instead inhibits thrombin and factor Xa.

questions.stem: These photographs show a dermatologic complication that can occur soon after starting an oral anticoagulant. What mechanism produces this skin damage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Transient hypercoagulability from rapid depletion of proteins C and S

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capillary fragility from vitamin K deficiency

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct cytotoxic drug effect on keratinocytes

explanation.summary: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis results from the short half-lives of the anticoagulant proteins C and S, which fall first and create a transient hypercoagulable state that thromboses small vessels and causes skin to die.
explanation.whyCorrect: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis results from the short half-lives of the anticoagulant proteins C and S, which fall first and create a transient hypercoagulable state that thromboses small vessels and causes skin to die.

questions.stem: The boxed factors in this figure indicate where warfarin exerts its effect on the clotting cascade. What is the biochemical basis for warfarin acting on exactly this set of factors?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They share a calcium-binding site independent of vitamin K

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are all synthesized by vascular endothelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are the only factors of the intrinsic pathway

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are all serine proteases uniquely cleaved by thrombin

explanation.summary: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, blocking gamma-carboxylation of the vitamin K-dependent factors II, VII, IX, and X and the regulatory proteins C and S, which are exactly the elements highlighted.
explanation.whyCorrect: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase, blocking gamma-carboxylation of the vitamin K-dependent factors II, VII, IX, and X and the regulatory proteins C and S, which are exactly the elements highlighted.

questions.stem: This figure illustrates how heparin acts on the coagulation cascade, marking its effect at factors Xa and IIa. Through what mechanism does heparin inhibit these factors?

choices.label: B
choices.text: It inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase

choices.label: C
choices.text: It chelates the calcium required by the cascade

choices.label: D
choices.text: It directly binds and cleaves thrombin

explanation.summary: Heparin works indirectly by activating endogenous antithrombin; the activated antithrombin then inhibits clotting factors Xa and IIa (thrombin) in the common pathway.
explanation.whyCorrect: Heparin works indirectly by activating endogenous antithrombin; the activated antithrombin then inhibits clotting factors Xa and IIa (thrombin) in the common pathway.
